items.title: Robbie Savage the panto villain puts scepticism aside to leave Leicester reeling
items.description: Peterborough’s new boss has long been a divisive figure but a stunning 3-1 win at struggling former club offered a glimpse of his fearless philosophyIt felt as though the stars had aligned when Robbie Savage’s first League One match in charge of Peterborough – his first EFL managerial role – happened to be at Leicester. He made his name here and forged a divisive and enduring reputation that has made him a permanent fixture in English football.Savage has long been a joker figure – an image born in his playing days, when he hurtled around midfield with long blond hair bouncing, launching into challenges that at one point made him the most booked player in Premier League history. A pantomime villain, a prankster and an eccentric who was once fined £10,000 by the Football Association – and two weeks’ wages by Leicester – for using the referee Graham Poll’s toilet before a match. items.title: Lionel Messi and Cristiano Ronaldo return to club action with strong performances after contrasting international breaks
items.description:
Lionel Messi and Cristiano Ronaldo returned to club action with goals after contrasting international breaks, with Messi scoring twice for Inter Miami and Ronaldo netting his 980th career goal for Al Nassr. 
Lionel Messi and Cristiano Ronaldo returned to club action this weekend after very different international breaks, and both marked the occasion with goals. Messi came back from an emotional farewell with the Argentina national team to score twice for Inter Miami on Saturday, October 10, while Ronaldo returned from a turbulent stint with Portugal to find the net for Al Nassr a day earlier.



Messi’s break was one of celebration. He arrived in Buenos Aires on October 2, missed the 7-0 win over Burkina Faso and said goodbye to the national team on October 6 with a goal and two assists in a 3-0 win over Benin in front of more than 85,000 fans. He left as Argentina’s most-capped player with 208 appearances, record scorer with 126 goals and record assist with 64 assists.



Four days later, he was back in Miami and the transition was seamless. Messi started and captained Inter Miami against DC United, where he scored a brace to reach 934 career goals. 



The two goals took his season total to 23 and kept him as the outright leader of the MLS Golden Boot race, while the win ended a five-match winless run for Inter Miami.




Simplemente Leo Messi. 🪄📽️ pic.twitter.com/QSB9eHK5Gg— Inter Miami CF (@InterMiamiCF) October 11, 2026




Ronaldo returns after a turbulent break



Cristiano Ronaldo’s international break was far more troubled. The Portuguese forward left the national team’s camp after a fallout with coach Jorge Jesus, having played only in the match against Wales on the first matchday of the UEFA Nations League.


        


After not getting any minutes against Norway on the second matchday, he decided to leave the camp, which sparked a major controversy over his future with Portugal. However, after a turbulent few weeks, the captain confirmed that he has not retired from international duty, and the federation has opened the door for his return in the next international window in November.



His return to Al Nassr on Friday, October 9, was a welcome change of atmosphere. The home fans chanted his name before kick-off and raised a banner in his honor that read “Greatness is earned,” and Ronaldo repaid them in the 23rd minute, pouncing on a rebound for his 980th career goal.




Yellow was made for greatness 💛🐐 pic.twitter.com/waRXHef8cR— AlNassr FC (@AlNassrFC_EN) October 9, 2026




Al Nassr won 3-0 and rose to 19 points, but Al Hilal’s win over Al Ittihad in Saturday’s clash lifted them to 21 and left Al Nassr third in the Saudi Pro League, two points behind the leaders and level on points with Al Qadsiah, which holds second place on goal difference. Ronaldo, meanwhile, now sits 20 goals away from becoming the first player to reach 1,000, while Messi, with 934, is 66 away.

items.title: Video: Lionel Messi reaches 934 career goals with brace for Inter Miami vs DC United at 2026 MLS season
items.description:
Lionel Messi scored his 22nd goal of the MLS season in Inter Miami’s 3-0 lead over DC United, his first match since saying goodbye to the Argentina national team. 
After saying goodbye to the Argentina national team, Lionel Messi returned to action with Inter Miami in the best possible way, scoring against DC United to extend his team’s lead to 3-0 at Nu Stadium.



Messi’s goal came from a pass by Luis Suárez, who is the star of the night for the home side. The Uruguayan had opened the scoring less than three minutes into the match and added a second goal before halftime, tapping in a rebound after Messi’s shot was saved by the goalkeeper. He then completed his performance by setting up Messi for the third, having been involved in all three of his team’s goals.



But the night was not over for Messi. In the 60th minute, the Argentine scored his second goal of the match and made it 4-0, dribbling past several DC United defenders before finishing across the goal with a precise shot. 



With those goals, the Argentine reached 23 goals this MLS season with the Herons and remains the outright leader of the MLS Golden Boot race, where he is aiming for a second consecutive award. He also has 13 assists, and with six regular-season matches still to play, he has plenty of time to extend his lead.




Luis Suarez to Messi 👏MLS best 22 goals for Messi. pic.twitter.com/GMvGvKdxYm— Major League Soccer (@MLS) October 11, 2026





Messi magic 🪄Two goals for the World Cup Champion. pic.twitter.com/PMA1l5tyZk— Major League Soccer (@MLS) October 11, 2026




Messi and Ronaldo’s race to 1,000 career goals



Messi’s brace against DC United took him to 934 career goals, including 672 with Barcelona, 126 with Argentina, 104 with Inter Miami and 32 with Paris Saint-Germain. Cristiano Ronaldo, meanwhile, scored his 980th goal on Friday, for Al Nassr against Al Diriyah, which leaves the Portuguese forward 20 goals away from the historic milestone while Messi still needs 66.


        


The gap between them is 46 goals, and the picture is different for each player. Messi, now 39, retired from international soccer after the win over Benin on October 6, so every goal from here on will come with Inter Miami, while Ronaldo, 41, still has both Al Nassr and the Portugal national team as options, although his recent fallout with Jorge Jesus has put his international future in question. 



Either way, Ronaldo is the clear favorite to become the first player to reach 1,000 goals, with Messi chasing the milestone as the only other player to have passed 900.

items.title: Jordan Henderson joins Cristiano Ronaldo in rare Premier League club with historic Chelsea performance
items.description:
Jordan Henderson became the oldest player in the Premier League to be directly involved in three goals in a match since Cristiano Ronaldo in 2022, as Chelsea beat Bournemouth 5-1. 
Jordan Henderson turned back the clock on Saturday scoring a brace and setting up another goal in Chelsea’s 5-1 win over Bournemouth at Stamford Bridge. The 36-year-old midfielder’s performance put him in rare company, as he became the oldest player for any club to be directly involved in three goals in a Premier League match since Cristiano Ronaldo did it in 2022.



Henderson wasted no time making his mark. He opened the scoring after just over a minute, sweeping in a first-time finish off the inside of the far post after Cole Palmer dribbled into the box and pulled the ball back.



Moments later he turned provider, helping set up Morgan Rogers for the second goal, giving him a goal and an assist inside two minutes and 29 seconds, a combination only Emile Heskey has managed faster in Premier League history.



The numbers behind the night go beyond the speed. According to Opta, Henderson is the oldest player to be directly involved in three goals in a Premier League game since Cristiano Ronaldo in April 2022, when the Portuguese star was 37 and scored a hat-trick against Norwich. At 36 years and 115 days, he also became the oldest Chelsea player ever to do so, overtaking a list that previously included Gianluca Vialli.




🫶 #CFC | #CHEBOU pic.twitter.com/NYjbuTg4bI— Chelsea FC (@ChelseaFC) October 10, 2026




For Henderson, the performance was also a statement for his team, as it helped Chelsea secure its first top-flight win since the end of August. João Pedro added two goals of his own, while Evanilson scored a consolation for Bournemouth, but the night belonged to the veteran midfielder.


        


Ronaldo continues to shine at 41



The comparison is also timely. Ronaldo, now 41, scored his 980th career goal for Al Nassr on Friday, October 9, opening the scoring in the 23rd minute of a 3-0 win over Al Diriyah. The goal came in his first match since leaving the Portugal camp and helped lift Al Nassr to 19 points, level with Al Qadsiah at the top of the Saudi Pro League table.



Ronaldo’s latest strike is his fourth of the Saudi Pro League season, and he is already looking to add to a strong record in the competition. He won the Golden Boot in 2023-24 with a league-record 35 goals and again in 2024-25 with 25, then scored 28 last season, when Julián Quiñones edged him out on the final day with 33. 



That means he has scored 88 league goals over his last three seasons, and he now chases a third Golden Boot. For now, though, Ivan Toney is a long way ahead with 11 goals, which leaves Ronaldo seven behind, but there is still plenty of the season left to close the gap.

items.title: Lamine Yamal’s 2026 Ballon d’Or hopes take major hit as new favorite takes over
items.description:
Despite another impressive campaign with Barcelona and Spain, the teenager is facing growing competition from a rival whose extraordinary goalscoring numbers have changed the bookmakers’ predictions. 
Lamine Yamal’s hopes of winning the 2026 Ballon d’Or have suffered a significant setback as the race for soccer’s most prestigious individual award enters its final weeks. Despite another impressive campaign with Barcelona and Spain, the teenager is facing growing competition from a rival whose extraordinary goalscoring numbers have changed the bookmakers’ predictions.



The award’s 70th-anniversary ceremony will take place on October 26 at the London Palladium, marking the first time the event has been held outside Paris. With voting having closed on September 28, attention has shifted toward the leading contenders and the performances that could ultimately decide the winner.



Yamal entered the final stage of the race as one of the strongest candidates after helping Barcelona win La Liga and playing a major role in Spain’s World Cup triumph. At just 19, he has an opportunity to become the youngest Ballon d’Or winner in history, adding another milestone to an already remarkable career.



His rise through the rankings has been rapid. Yamal finished eighth in 2024 before becoming the runner-up in 2025 behind Ousmane Dembele, while also winning consecutive Kopa Trophies as the world’s best young player.



Lamine Yamal of FC Barcelona reacts



His 2025-26 campaign further strengthened his credentials, with 24 goals and 18 assists in 45 appearances for club and country, according to the supplied reports. Barcelona’s domestic success and Spain’s international achievements give him a compelling case, although the latest odds suggest that individual statistics could prove decisive.



Harry Kane emerges as the leading contender



The player now heading the bookmakers’ rankings is Harry Kane, whose prolific season for Bayern Munich and England has made him the favorite to claim his first Ballon d’Or. The England captain reportedly scored 73 goals in 65 competitive appearances during the 2025-26 campaign, including 61 for Bayern and 12 for his national team.



Kane also collected major honors with the German giant, winning the Bundesliga, the DFB-Pokal and the European Golden Shoe after scoring 36 league goals. His individual production has attracted strong endorsements, including support from the club’s honorary president Uli Hoeness. “He would have deserved it enormously. If he doesn’t deserve it this year, then when?” Hoeness said, according to Münchner Abendzeitung.



Harry Kane of Bayern Munich.



England coach Thomas Tuchel has also praised Kane’s development, saying: “He is getting better and better.” Kane’s goalscoring record has helped him move ahead of Yamal in the betting market, even though the Spaniard has enjoyed considerable team success.



The latest odds reveal changing race



According to the UK’s leading betting odds comparison website Oddschecker, Kane is the clear favorite at best odds of 5/4, while Yamal follows at 2/1. Those prices imply approximate chances of 44% and 33%, respectively, although bookmaker odds are estimates rather than guarantees of the final result. The movement in the market has been particularly notable.



Several bookmakers shortened Kane’s odds as the voting deadline approached, while Yamal drifted from shorter prices toward 2/1, suggesting that confidence in the Englishman had increased. Recent international performances may have contributed to the shift. Kane scored twice against Czechia on October 6, while Yamal failed to register a goal or assist in Spain’s 2-1 victory over Croatia, although one match alone cannot determine the outcome of an award covering an entire season.



RankPlayerOdds1.Harry Kane4/52.Lamine Yamal6/53.Kylian Mbappe20/14.Lionel Messi22/15.Rodri40/15.Michael Olise40/17.Khvicha Kvaratskhelia50/18.Ousmane Dembélé100/1



Kylian Mbappe is another major contender, sitting third in the reported odds at 14/1. The Real Madrid forward won the World Cup Golden Boot with ten goals and finished as the top scorer in both La Liga and the Champions League, but his case has been weakened by the club’s failure to win a major trophy.



Rodri, the 2024 Ballon d’Or winner, is also in contention after captaining Spain to World Cup glory and collecting the tournament’s Golden Ball. Lionel Messi, an eight-time winner, remains among the outsiders, while reigning champion Dembele faces a difficult path to retaining his title.

items.title: Cristiano Ronaldo makes powerful admission after 980th goal as Al-Nassr captain can’t hold back tears in emotional return after Portugal drama
items.description:
Ronaldo helped his club secure a convincing victory, while an emotional moment with supporters showed just how much the past few days may have weighed on the Portuguese superstar. 
Cristiano Ronaldo returned to Al-Nassr amid a storm of controversy surrounding his departure from Portugal’s national team camp, but the reception waiting for him in Riyadh offered a powerful contrast. The 41-year-old forward helped his club secure a convincing victory, while an emotional moment with supporters showed just how much the past few days may have weighed on the Portuguese superstar.



Al-Nassr defeated Al-Diriyah 3-0 in the Saudi Pro League, with Ronaldo opening the scoring on his first club appearance since the international dispute. The goal brought his extraordinary career tally to 980, leaving him only 20 away from the landmark of 1,000 official goals.



Ronaldo made his presence felt in the 23rd minute, reacting quickest after the goalkeeper parried a shot from Kingsley Coman. The Portuguese forward converted the rebound to give Ange Postecoglou’s players the lead and register his fourth league goal of the campaign.



Samu Costa doubled the advantage with a header from Joao Felix’s corner before Coman completed the scoring in the 77th minute, finishing a counterattack. The result strengthened Al-Nassr’s position near the top of the Saudi Pro League table, with the club collecting 19 points from its first eight matches.









For the 41-year-old superstar, the goal was another step towards a milestone that has increasingly defined the closing stages of his career. He now needs 20 more goals to reach 1,000, a target he continues to pursue while competing for silverware with Al-Nassr.



Al-Nassr supporters give their captain an emotional welcome



The biggest talking point, however, came after the final whistle. Post-game video footage showed Ronaldo wearing an Al-Nassr scarf, raising his hands towards the crowd and appearing tearful as supporters celebrated their captain. The home crowd had already made its support clear before kick-off, displaying a banner that read, “Greatness is earned, CR7, all-time top scorer in football history.”



VAMOS 🐐 pic.twitter.com/qscAi87Obp— Al Nassr Zone (@TheNassrZone) October 9, 2026 



The reception appeared particularly meaningful given the criticism and uncertainty surrounding Ronaldo following his departure from Portugal’s national team camp. The timing could suggest that the supporters’ reception may have affected him, especially after a difficult international break. Ronaldo’s emotional homecoming followed a public disagreement with Portugal head coach Jorge Jesus over his role during the international break.



The forward was reportedly promised playing time against Norway but remained an unused substitute, despite warming up during the match. The federation confirmed that disciplinary proceedings had been opened, leaving Ronaldo facing uncertainty over the potential consequences. His return to Al-Nassr therefore came at a moment when his club career offered a more immediate focus than the unresolved situation with Portugal.



Cristiano Ronaldo couldn’t hold back the tears.😢 https://t.co/VquCnabrgC— The Nassr Tribune™️ (@AlNassrTribune) October 9, 2026




What Ronaldo’s emotional moment could mean



Ronaldo has built his career around extraordinary standards, fierce competitiveness and an intense desire to win.  A more measured reading is that a turbulent international break, a successful return to club action, and a strong show of affection from Al-Nassr supporters created an emotionally charged occasion.



        View this post on Instagram            




The images offer a glimpse of a more vulnerable moment, although Ronaldo has not publicly confirmed why he appeared in tears. His brief post-match message gave little away about the controversy. “Job done. On to the next one!” he wrote on social media, suggesting that his immediate attention had shifted back to soccer.

items.title: Cristiano Ronaldo hit with preventive suspension as Portugal investigates shock camp exit: Possible ban length and when he could return to national team
items.description:
Consequently, his international future remains temporarily uncertain while authorities formally review the circumstances surrounding his unauthorized departure from the training camp. 
Cristiano Ronaldo’s tenure with the Portugal national team has entered a challenging phase following the escalation of his dispute with manager Jorge Jesus into an official disciplinary matter. The Portuguese Football Federation (FPF) has confirmed a provisional suspension for the 41-year-old captain. Consequently, his international future remains temporarily uncertain while authorities formally review the circumstances surrounding his unauthorized departure from the training camp.



The FPF confirmed this Saturday, October 10, 2026, that disciplinary proceedings had been opened against Ronaldo following incidents reported on October 7. The case has been classified as urgent and referred to the federation’s Disciplinary Investigation Committee, which will determine the final consequences of his actions.



In its official statement, the federation said: “Without prejudice to the automatic provisional suspension to which he was subject until the date the proceedings were opened, a non-automatic provisional suspension has been imposed on him, with the urgency of the proceedings acknowledged.”



No final punishment has been announced, and the FPF has prohibited the publication of further details while the investigation remains ongoing. The provisional suspension means Ronaldo’s case must be resolved before his availability for Portugal can be established.



Cristiano Ronaldo of Portugal.



How the dispute with Jorge Jesus began



The controversy followed Ronaldo’s frustration at being left on the bench during Portugal’s 2-1 victory over Norway. The forward reportedly expected to receive around 30 minutes of playing time after discussions with Jesus, but despite warming up, he was never introduced.



Ronaldo also claimed that a second disagreement arose over how the coach would explain the decision publicly. Feeling that promises had been broken, the 41-year-old left Portugal’s training camp before the subsequent match against Denmark, turning a disagreement over selection into a major issue for the national team.



The situation was particularly striking because Jesus had previously coached Ronaldo at Al-Nassr before taking charge of Portugal. Their professional relationship had appeared to offer a foundation for cooperation, but the dispute has now placed both men under intense scrutiny.



Head coach Jorge Jesus interacts with Cristiano Ronaldo of Al Nassr. (Yasser Bakhsh/Getty Images)



The possible ban length revealed



The key question is how long Ronaldo could remain suspended from international duty. According to reports citing Portuguese disciplinary regulations, the potential punishment ranges from one to six months, with a financial penalty also possible.



However, the final sanction could be considerably shorter. Sports lawyer Goncalo Almeida has explained that Ronaldo’s admission of responsibility and apology may qualify him for a reduction under Article 244 of the FPF regulations.



“The most important factors that could work in Cristiano Ronaldo’s favour are his full admission of leaving the camp and his apology, his clean disciplinary record, and his long-standing service to the Portuguese national team,” Almeida told A Bola.



Cristiano Ronaldo of Portugal.



Under the best-case scenario described in the reports, a minimum one-month suspension could be reduced to 15 days, accompanied by a fine of approximately €255 ($268). Ronaldo’s role as captain could count against him, however, because the federation may view his responsibilities as making the unauthorized departure more serious.



When could Ronaldo return for Portugal?



The timing of the disciplinary decision will determine Ronaldo’s next possible appearance for his country. A suspension lasting longer than one month could rule him out of Portugal’s November Nations League fixtures against Denmark and Wales, while a shorter punishment could give him a chance to return sooner.



If the minimum sanction is reduced to 15 days and the time already served under the provisional suspension is counted, Ronaldo could theoretically become available before the November international window. That remains a possibility rather than a confirmed outcome, as the disciplinary committee has yet to issue its verdict.



Players of Portugal pose for a team photograph 



The federation will also have to consider the wider relationship between Ronaldo and Jesus as Portugal prepares for future international commitments. Reports have suggested that FPF president Pedro Proenca wants the dispute resolved, with March 2027 emerging as a potential target for Ronaldo’s return if reconciliation and the disciplinary process progress favourably.

items.title: Atletico Madrid takes sarcastic jab at Real Madrid over Fede Valverde’s rapid recovery
items.description:
Atlético Madrid has taken a sarcastic jab at Real Madrid over Fede Valverde’s rapid recovery, just weeks after the club announced a third-degree ankle sprain. 
Atletico Madrid has taken a sarcastic jab at Real Madrid over Federico Valverde’s rapid recovery, using social media to poke fun at the speed of his return from injury. The Uruguayan midfielder was named in Real Madrid’s squad for Saturday’s match against Villarreal, roughly three weeks after the club announced a third-degree ankle sprain suffered in the Madrid derby.



On Friday, Atletico posted on its official X account that it wanted to congratulate Real Madrid for “continuing to make history” by proving that “100% of the global medical community was wrong”.



The message was also accompanied by hashtags such as #MiracleRecovery and #Grade3Sprain, a clear reference to the usual timeline for that kind of injury, which typically keeps players out for two to three months. Valverde, however, returned to training with the group and was included in the squad list just 17 days after the medical report.



Valverde was hurt in the derby on September 20, which Atletico won 2-1 at the Metropolitano, after a hard challenge from Kang-in Lee in the first half. The midfielder finished the game, but the worry only set in once the final whistle blew and swelling appeared around his ankle. Two days later, on September 22, the club confirmed a third-degree sprain, with his recovery listed as “pending evolution.”




Queremos felicitar al @RealMadrid por seguir haciendo historia al demostrar que el 100% de la comunidad médica mundial estaba equivocada. #RecuperaciónMilagrosa #ParteMédico #EsguinceGrado3 #HistoriaQueTúHiciste— Atlético de Madrid (@Atleti) October 9, 2026




Real Madrid kept his return under wraps until it announced the squad for the Villarreal match, and Jose Mourinho made clear on Friday that nothing is decided yet. The coach called Valverde “the doubt” and said the club would define on Saturday how to handle him, so it remains unclear whether the midfielder will start or return from the bench.


        


Madrid’s clubs can’t afford to lose sight of Barcelona



The sarcasm comes with real stakes in the LaLiga table. Barcelona is perfect so far, with seven wins from seven matches and 21 points, which gives it a comfortable cushion at the top. Atletico Madrid sits second on 16 points, level with Real Betis, while Real Madrid is fourth on 15 after five wins and two defeats.



That gap explains why both sides need to win this weekend. Real Madrid hosts Villarreal on Saturday, October 10, while Atlético travels to face Alavés on the same day, and Barcelona is also in action against Getafe.

items.title: Cristiano Ronaldo powers Al Nassr to victory, but the Saudi Pro League Golden Boot still seems far away
items.description:
Cristiano Ronaldo scored his 980th career goal in Al Nassr’s 3-0 win over Al Diriyah, but he remains well behind Ivan Toney in the Saudi Pro League Golden Boot race. 
Cristiano Ronaldo scored in Al Nassr’s 3-0 win over Al Diriyah on Friday, October 9, in his first match since leaving the Portugal camp. The goal was his 980th as a professional, but the Saudi Pro League scoring chart shows he is still well behind the leaders.



Ronaldo opened the scoring in the 23rd minute at Al-Awwal Park, pouncing on a rebound in front of an empty net after goalkeeper Waleed Abdullah could only parry Kingsley Coman’s powerful strike. Samu Costa made it 2-0 in the 35th minute, heading home a corner delivered by Joao Felix, while Coman wrapped up the win in the 77th minute.



The match carried extra weight for Ronaldo after the turmoil of recent days, where he left the Portugal camp following his fallout with coach Jorge Jesus. The home fans made their feelings clear before kick-off, chanting his name and raising a banner in his honor, and he repaid them with the opening goal.



The result also keeps Al Nassr in the title race. The win took them to 19 points, level with leaders Al Qadsiah but behind on goal difference. However, Al Hilal or Al Ittihad could overtake both with a win in their clash on Saturday, October 10.




Job done. On to the next one! 💪🏽 pic.twitter.com/lwKjjmcOBG— Cristiano Ronaldo (@Cristiano) October 9, 2026




Golden Boot still out of reach



The scoring table shows how much ground Ronaldo still has to make up. Ivan Toney leads the Saudi Pro League with 11 goals in eight appearances, well ahead of the rest. Francisco Trincão, Mateo Retegui and Alexandre Lacazette follow with five each.


        


A little further down, Ronaldo is listed with four goals in seven appearances, leaving him well behind the leader of the table. The Portuguese star is not the only player in the Saudi Pro League with four goals, which makes the race for the Golden Boot tighter and more intense.



Al Qadsiah’s Julián Quiñones, Al Ittihad’s George Ilenikhena, Steven Bergwijn and Youssef En-Nesyri, and Al Hilal’s Sergej Milinković-Savić are all level with him, so the race behind Toney is crowded. At 41, Ronaldo would need a big run of goals to close the gap, and Toney has set a pace that is hard to match.

items.title: How many goals does Cristiano Ronaldo need to reach 1,000? Updated tally after Al-Nassr’s Saudi Pro League match vs Diriyah
items.description:
His latest appearance in the Saudi Pro League against Diriyah offered an opportunity to respond on the pitch, while his ongoing dispute with national team coach Jorge Jesus remains unresolved. 
Cristiano Ronaldo has returned to club soccer with Al-Nassr after a turbulent international break with Portugal, and the 41-year-old forward has once again turned his attention toward one of the biggest milestones of his career. His latest appearance in the Saudi Pro League against Diriyah offered an opportunity to respond on the pitch, while his ongoing dispute with national team coach Jorge Jesus remains unresolved.



Ronaldo left Portugal’s training camp after being an unused substitute during the 2-1 victory over Norway, having previously started the 1-0 win against Wales. The decision ended an extraordinary run of approximately 18 years without being left unused on the bench in a competitive Portugal match, adding another chapter to the controversy surrounding his international future.



The 41-year-old superstar has now returned to action as Al-Nassr hosted Diriyah at Al-Awwal Park in Riyadh on Friday, October 9, 2026, in Matchday 8 of the Saudi Pro League. The fixture marked his first competitive appearance since the Portugal controversy and gave him a chance to redirect the attention toward his performances for the Saudi club.



Al-Nassr entered the match sitting third in the league standings with 16 points from seven games, having recorded five wins, one draw and one defeat. The club had scored 16 goals and conceded seven, keeping it firmly in the early title race behind Al-Hilal and Al-Ittihad.



Cristiano Ronaldo, Al Nassr’s captain



Diriyah, meanwhile, arrived in eighth place with 11 points, following an encouraging start to its first Saudi Pro League campaign. The two clubs had already met in the King’s Cup in August, when the Knight of Najd secured a 4-1 victory.



Ronaldo scores again as the race to 1,000 continues



Ronaldo entered the match having scored 979 official goals in 1,336 senior appearances for club and country. At 41 years old, the five-time Ballon d’Or winner continues to produce at an extraordinary level, with his pursuit of 1,000 goals becoming one of the biggest individual storylines in soccer.



The Portuguese made his return count by scoring against Diriyah, taking his remarkable career tally to 980 goals. The latest strike moved him another step closer to a milestone that has become one of the defining storylines of the final stage of his playing career.



RONALDO TAKES THE LEAD FOR AL-NASSR… IT IS 1-0 🐐🟡 pic.twitter.com/IqdSeYRDyT— All About SPL 🔔 🇸🇦 (@Saudifutbol) October 9, 2026 



That leaves the veteran forward needing 20 more goals to reach 1,000 official career goals. His previous strike against Abha in September had brought him to 979, meaning the Diriyah goal added another milestone to his extraordinary record across club and international soccer.



The achievement also provided a timely reminder of Ronaldo’s continued importance to Al-Nassr. Despite the noise surrounding his Portugal departure, the forward remains a central figure in the club’s attacking plans under coach Ange Postecoglou.



The next step toward soccer history



Ronaldo’s goal against Diriyah has brought him to 980 career goals, leaving him 20 short of the 1,000 mark. At 41, he continues to chase a target that would represent one of the most extraordinary individual achievements in the history of the sport.



For now, Al-Nassr will hope his scoring form helps the club maintain pressure on the teams above it in the league standings. The Portugal controversy may continue away from the pitch, but Ronaldo has delivered another reminder that his pursuit of soccer history remains very much alive.

items.title: Video: Cristiano Ronaldo returns from Portugal turmoil with 980th career goal in Al Nassr vs Al Diriyah
items.description:
Cristiano Ronaldo scored his 980th career goal in Al Nassr’s match against Al Diriyah, pouncing on a rebound after a Kingsley Coman shot, and is now 20 goals away from 1,000. 
After a turbulent week with the Portugal national team, in which Cristiano Ronaldo left the national team’s camp in the middle of the UEFA Nations League international window, the forward returned to action with Al Nassr in the best possible way.



With the Matchday 8 Saudi Pro League game between Al Nassr and Al Diriyah tied at 0-0, Kingsley Coman unleashed a powerful shot that the goalkeeper saved, and Ronaldo pounced on the rebound to score the first goal of the match.



With this strike, Cristiano now has 980 career goals and is just 20 away from becoming the first player in soccer history to reach the 1,000-goal mark. It is his fourth goal of the season, all of them scored in the Saudi Pro League.



Ronaldo’s goal comes at a good moment for the forward, who returned to club action after a turbulent week with Portugal that ended with him leaving the national team camp. 



CRISTIANO RONALDO IS STILL THE BEST FINISHER IN THE WORLD AT 41! pic.twitter.com/FekoCRZkPG— The Nassr Tribune™️ (@AlNassrTribune) October 9, 2026 



Back on the pitch with Al Nassr, he answered with a goal that moves him closer to the 1,000-goal milestone and gives him a boost of confidence after a difficult spell away from the club.


        


Al Nassr fighting for the top spots



If Al Nassr hold on to their partial lead, the three points would take them from 16 to 19 and put them level with Al Qadsiah at the top of the Saudi Pro League table. Al Qadsiah reached that mark earlier on Friday with a 5-0 win over Al Khaleej, so goal difference would decide who sits first.



A win would also put Al Nassr one point ahead of Al Hilal, who have 18 and have yet to play their Round 8 match, and two ahead of Al Ittihad, who have 17 and will face each other in the Clásico later in the round. For a team that came into the match third after a difficult run of results, it would be an important step toward getting their season back on track.

items.title: Report: Cristiano Ronaldo could reunite with Martinez at Al Nassr as Postecoglou’s future comes into question
items.description:
Cristiano Ronaldo could reportedly reunite with Roberto Martínez at Al Nassr, according to a Saudi TV program that claims Ange Postecoglou’s future is in danger. 
Cristiano Ronaldo could reportedly be reunited with a familiar coach at Al Nassr, as Ange Postecoglou’s future at the club has come into question just three months after his arrival. According to a report from the Saudi television program Nadeena Show, the Australian manager’s position is in danger and former Portugal coach Roberto Martínez could be the one to replace him.



The claim comes after a difficult stretch for Postecoglou, who joined in July on a two-year contract to replace Jorge Jesus. The Australian guided Al Nassr to five straight wins in all competitions and was named the Saudi Pro League’s Manager of the Month for August, a start that made him an early success story in Riyadh.



The team was unable to sustain that form, however, losing 2-1 to Al Ittihad and drawing 1-1 with Al Khaleej before suffering a 4-0 defeat to Al Ain in the AFC Champions League Elite, the heaviest loss Ronaldo has experienced since arriving in Saudi Arabia in 2023.



Amid this difficult stretch for Al Nassr, the idea has emerged that Martínez could take over the team, where he has been linked to the club before. Reports earlier this year said the Spanish coach was in talks to take charge of Al Nassr after the World Cup, although Postecoglou ultimately ended up being the one chosen for the job.



Cristiano Ronaldo of Portugal celebrates victory with Roberto Martinez. (Getty Images)



For now, Al Nassr sit third in the Saudi Pro League with 16 points, two behind leaders Al Hilal, and Postecoglou will be on the touchline on Friday when the team host Al Diriyah.


        


Saudi Arabia shut the door on Martínez



Al Nassr might not be the only Saudi job Martínez has been linked to since leaving Portugal. Reports in recent weeks claimed the Spanish coach had already reached an agreement to take over the Saudi national team, a story that appeared to threaten the position of Georgios Donis, but the federation quickly stepped in to put an end to the speculation.



“The manager is continuing with the national team, and no decision has been taken regarding a change in the coaching staff,” the Saudi Arabian Football Federation said in an official statement, while urging media outlets to verify information through official channels.



Donis had good reasons to feel under pressure. The Greek coach took charge in late April, replacing Hervé Renard on a contract that runs through July 2027, and his first big test did not go well, as Saudi Arabia drew with Uruguay and Cape Verde and lost 4-0 to Spain, finishing last in their World Cup group and failing to advance for the sixth straight tournament.



But the mood around him has changed since Tuesday, when Saudi Arabia beat the UAE 2-0 in Jeddah to win the Gulf Cup for the fourth time in their history, ending a drought of more than two decades. That title appears to have secured Donis’s position, at least for now, and he will be expected to build on that momentum ahead of the 2027 AFC Asian Cup.

Al Nassr confirmed lineup
With Cristiano Ronaldo back and after a rough moment with the Portugal national team, Al Nassr are set to display a strong lineup to face Diriyah and secure three vital points at home.
Al Nassr confirmed starting XI (4-4-2): Bento, Nawaf Bu Washl, Awad Aman, Samú Costa, Mohamed Simakan, Iñigo Martínez, Kingsley Coman, Abdullah Al Khaibari, Cristiano Ronaldo, João Félix, Sadio Mané. Coach: Ange Postecoglou.
Diriyah confirmed lineup
Diriyah have had a solid start of the season with three victories, two draws, and to defeated. However, their visit to Al Nassr is one of the toughest games they have faced so far and getting points on the road won’t be an easy task at all.
Diriyah confirmed starting XI (4-2-3-1): Waleed Abdullah, Abdulaziz Al Faraj, Hussain Al Sibyani, Qasem Lajami, Berat Djimsiti, Chancel Mbemba, Enzo Millot, Idrissa Gueye, Darwin Núñez, Óscar Rodríguez, Adil Boulbina. Coach: Bruno Miguel Silva do Nascimento.

items.title: Cristiano Ronaldo’s reported Al-Nassr 20% stake takes fresh twist as ownership truth comes to light
items.description:
While the Portuguese superstar has been linked to a major business opportunity involving the Saudi Pro League side, a fresh clarification has challenged the claims surrounding his alleged involvement. 
Cristiano Ronaldo’s future at Al-Nassr has become the subject of renewed speculation as reports about the club’s ownership and potential private investment continue to circulate. While the Portuguese superstar has been linked to a major business opportunity involving the Saudi Pro League side, a fresh clarification has challenged the claims surrounding his alleged involvement.



Saudi journalist Khaled Al-Rasheed has stressed that the ownership situation is different from what some reports have suggested. The distinction matters as Saudi Arabia explores new investment opportunities for its leading soccer clubs.



Al-Nassr is currently 100% owned by Saudi Arabia’s Public Investment Fund (PIF), according to the clarification attributed to Al-Rasheed. The claim directly contradicts suggestions circulating in September that Ronaldo had already secured a 20% stake in the club.



PIF initially acquired a 75% stake in Al-Nassr in 2023 as part of Saudi Arabia’s Sports Clubs Investment and Privatization Project under Vision 2030. The remaining 25% was held by a nonprofit foundation linked to the Ministry of Sport before reportedly transferring to PIF in August 2026, giving the sovereign wealth fund complete ownership.



Cristiano Ronaldo of Al Nassr celebrates with the Saudi Pro League Trophy.



The Portuguese veteran joined the club  in early 2023 and later extended his contract into 2027, becoming one of the central figures in Saudi soccer’s international expansion. However, he has not been confirmed as a shareholder in Al-Nassr’s current ownership structure.


        


The reported 20% opportunity behind the rumours



The speculation appears to have intensified after reports emerged in September 2026 that a consortium was discussing the possibility of acquiring a stake in Al-Nassr. According to reports attributed to A Bola and Asharq Bloomberg, the proposed group could include RedBird Capital Partners, former Al-Nassr president Ibrahim Al-Muhaidib and Saudi Media Company chairman Mohammed Al-Khuraiji.



Ronaldo was reportedly linked to the discussions, with claims that a clause in his playing contract could give him priority rights to acquire up to 20% of the club if it becomes available to private investors. However, the reported clause and consortium discussions have not resulted in a publicly confirmed transaction.



The proposed investment group was reportedly considering a combined commitment of around $500 million, with individual investors potentially contributing at least $100 million. Negotiations were said to be ongoing, but neither PIF nor the other parties had announced a completed deal in the supplied reports.



PIF and Kingdom Holding Company’s representatives arrange deal over Al Hilal.



Why Ronaldo’s reported stake needs clarification



The key distinction is between having a potential contractual opportunity to purchase shares and actually owning them. A reported right to acquire equity in the future does not establish present-day ownership, and the available information does not confirm that Ronaldo has exercised such a right.


        


The confusion highlights the difficulty of separating confirmed developments from speculation as Saudi Pro League soccer moves toward greater private investment. PIF’s involvement has helped transform the league by attracting international stars and funding ambitious recruitment projects, while privatization initiatives could introduce new investors and commercial partners.



Cristiano Ronaldo of Al Nassr lifts the Saudi Pro League Trophy



For Al-Nassr, a future ownership change could bring additional capital and a different business structure. But until the relevant parties confirm an agreement, the club’s ownership remains with PIF.



Although the 41-year-old superstar has not been confirmed as an Al-Nassr shareholder, he has reportedly pursued other opportunities in soccer investment. The supplied reports state that he holds a 25% stake in Spanish club UD Almería through his CR7 Sports Investments vehicle, giving him an existing connection to club ownership outside Saudi Arabia.

items.title: Raphinha to miss Barcelona’s next two games as Hansi Flick explains injury concerns
items.description:
Raphinha will miss Barcelona’s next two games against Getafe and Galatasaray, with Hansi Flick opting for a cautious approach due to the Brazilian’s injury history. 
Barcelona will have to navigate the next stretch of their schedule without one of their most important players, as Hansi Flick confirmed that Raphinha will miss the club’s next two games. 



The Brazilian winger will sit out the LaLiga match against Getafe on Saturday and the Champions League trip to Galatasaray in Istanbul on Tuesday, with the German coach opting for a cautious approach as the forward recovers from a thigh problem.



Speaking at Friday’s pre-match press conference, Flick explained that the situation does not appear to be serious, but that the club cannot afford to take risks. “It is not a major injury, but it is something that must be taken into account because he had many injuries,” the coach explained. Flick also noted that the tests showed something, but not a significant injury, recalling that Raphinha suffered three problems in the same area last season.



The injury occurred while Raphinha was on international duty with Brazil. He scored a penalty in the 4-2 win over Australia on September 29, but was substituted at halftime because of muscle discomfort, which led him to leave the national team’s camp and miss the 4-0 win over India.




🗣️ Hansi Flick on Raphinha: “It’s not an injury, but we have to be careful because he had three injuries last year, so we need to look after him. He won’t be available tomorrow or against Galatasaray.” pic.twitter.com/T8D4TfITKf— FC Barcelona (@FCBarcelona) October 9, 2026




The Brazilian Football Confederation said that medical examinations revealed a small muscle edema in the posterior region of his right thigh, and tests ruled out a muscle tear.


        


The absence is a significant one for Barcelona, since Raphinha has been in outstanding form this season, scoring 14 goals in his first eight appearances across all competitions as the club won its first seven LaLiga matches.



Gabriel Jesus set to replace Raphinha



With Raphinha unavailable, Gabriel Jesus will take his place in the starting lineup against Getafe. It would be the first start for the Brazilian striker since he joined Barcelona from Arsenal this summer, as he has so far appeared in four matches, all off the bench.



“The idea is for Gabriel Jesus to start. He has improved a lot, he has adapted, he understands our style of play and he is very strong inside the box. He has trained very well these three weeks and he is ready,” the German coach explained.



Despite playing just 41 minutes in total, Jesus has already scored two goals, one against Racing Santander and another against Feyenoord in the Champions League, which came only seven minutes after he stepped on the pitch.

items.title: Cristiano Ronaldo’s Al Nassr tie down four young talents and add two signings to strengthen youth ranks
items.description:
Cristiano Ronaldo’s Al Nassr have moved to secure the future of some of their most promising young players, announcing contract renewals for four talents from their youth ranks. The club confirmed the news on its official X account on Thursday, October 8, adding two new signings to reinforce its youth squads as well. The four […] 
Cristiano Ronaldo’s Al Nassr have moved to secure the future of some of their most promising young players, announcing contract renewals for four talents from their youth ranks. The club confirmed the news on its official X account on Thursday, October 8, adding two new signings to reinforce its youth squads as well.



The four players who have signed new deals are Abdulrahman Al-Anzi, Yousef Al-Tahan, Fawaz Al-Mashhour and Abdulrahman Sufyani, a player that Al Hilal reportedly tried to sign on two occasions.



This is the second renewal for Sufyani, who was rewarded for his strong performances with Al Nassr‘s U-21 side in last season’s Saudi Elite League. Al Nassr had previously renewed the young player in December 2025 on a three-year deal, according to Saudi media, a move that also came amid reports of interest from their rival.



Alongside the renewals, the club announced the signing of Tunisian Yassine Salam from Al Ettifaq to strengthen its youth categories, as well as goalkeeper Abdulhadi Al-Alwan, who joins on loan from Al Fateh until the end of the current season.




وقعت شركة نادي #النصر عقدًا احترافيًا مع اللاعب التونسي ياسين سلاّم "مواليد المملكة العربية السعودية" ✍️قادمًا من نادي الاتفاق.متمنين له التوفيق مع ناديه #العالمي 💛 pic.twitter.com/3h0KxgDM2L— ألعاب النصر المختلفة و الفئات السنية (@Alnassr_SG) October 8, 2026




Al-Alwan is already part of the first-team picture, as Ange Postecoglou has called him up for Friday’s Saudi Pro League match against Al Diriyah to cover for injuries in goal.


        


Youth side struggles in the U-21 league



The reinforcements arrive at a difficult time for Al Nassr’s U-21 team, who have been struggling since the beginning of the season. The club sit 14th in the Saudi U-21 Elite League with six points from two wins and two defeats, which puts them at risk of missing out on the quarterfinals at the end of the campaign.



The announcements also come as the club’s financial restrictions have reportedly been lifted, according to reports on Thursday, although there has been no official confirmation. If that is the case, Al Nassr could now look to go after free agents in the market, something that was not possible while the restrictions were in place.



Ultimately, the renewals and new signings show that Al Nassr are trying to build for the long term, protecting their most promising young players while adding reinforcements to a youth side that needs to improve. 



With Sufyani and the rest of the group now secured, the club will be hoping that investment in its academy starts to pay off, both in the U-21 league standings and in producing players who can eventually make the jump to Ronaldo’s first team.

items.title: Cristiano Ronaldo gets defensive boost as Al Nassr recover Mohamed Simakan ahead of Al Diriyah clash
items.description:
Al Nassr received a timely boost in defense ahead of their next Saudi Pro League match, as Mohamed Simakan is back in contention to face Al Diriyah. The French center back had been a doubt after suffering a muscle strain, but he has now passed the team's fitness tests, which should give Ange Postecoglou some […] 
Al Nassr received a timely boost in defense ahead of their next Saudi Pro League match, as Mohamed Simakan is back in contention to face Al Diriyah. The French center back had been a doubt after suffering a muscle strain, but he has now passed the team’s fitness tests, which should give Ange Postecoglou some relief as Cristiano Ronaldo and company return to league action on Friday, October 9.



According to Saudi newspaper Arriyadiyah, Simakan took part in the full team training session on Thursday, the day before the match, and has entered Postecoglou’s plans. 



His recovery could have been a real problem for the coach, since the doubts about his fitness threatened to leave Al Nassr short in defense, but the Frenchman’s return gives the team a key piece at a moment when it needs stability at the back.



The match against Al Diriyah, scheduled for 2 p.m. ET, comes at an important point for Al Nassr in the standings. The club sits third in the Saudi Pro League with 16 points, two behind leaders Al Hilal and one behind Al Ittihad, who occupy second place with 17.




Friday night. AlAwwal Park. You know where to be 💛🏟️ pic.twitter.com/EhVXvzFPH5— AlNassr FC (@AlNassrFC_EN) October 8, 2026




Postecoglou’s side is also coming off a 4-0 loss to Al Ain in its last outing, so a solid defensive performance against a newly promoted side would help them turn the page. The game also marks Ronaldo’s return to club action following a turbulent international break with Portugal, which ended with the forward leaving the national team camp.


        


Several other absences force changes for Al Nassr



Simakan’s return comes with some bad news for Postecoglou, as Abdulelah Al-Amri has been left out of the squad due to fatigue after winning the Gulf Cup with Saudi Arabia, while Abdulrahman Ghareeb has also been excluded because he is not physically ready to play, according to Arriyadiyah.



The club will also be short in goal, so Postecoglou has called up young goalkeeper Abdulhadi Al-Alwan to cover for the injuries to Nawaf Al-Aqidi, Raghad Al-Najjar and Mubarak Al-Buainain.



Nawaf Boushal, Abdullah Al-Khaibari and Abdullah Al-Hamdan, who also won the Gulf Cup with Saudi Arabia, arrived at the club’s headquarters alongside Al-Amri, though the report does not specify their status for the match.

items.title: Christian Pulisic’s role for Milan’s clash vs Sassuolo takes intriguing turn as Ruben Amorim’s lineup begins to emerge ahead of packed October
items.description:
Battered by injuries and facing a relentless fixture list, the Rossoneri mastermind is on the precipice of a profound tactical metamorphosis, where the role of the American talisman hangs delicately in the balance. 
A veil of intrigue surrounds Christian Pulisic as Milan braces for a looming battle against Sassuolo. With the international break in the rearview mirror, Ruben Amorim must forge a path through a grueling, unforgiving October gauntlet. Battered by injuries and facing a relentless fixture list, the Rossoneri mastermind is on the precipice of a profound tactical metamorphosis, where the role of the American talisman hangs delicately in the balance.



Milan has started the league campaign strongly under Amorim, collecting three wins and two draws from its opening five Serie A matches. The victory over Lecce before the break was particularly encouraging, with Pulisic, Diego Moreira and Adrien Rabiot all finding the net in a convincing 3-0 win.



The Rossoneri now return to action on Sunday, October 11, against Sassuolo at the Mapei Stadium. The match begins an extremely demanding month in which the Rossoneri are expected to play for 21 points across just 28 days, making squad rotation increasingly important.



Amorim has already shown that he wants his side to evolve tactically, and this weekend could provide another example. The Portuguese coach is reportedly considering a more attacking setup while still trying to maintain enough defensive balance to deal with Sassuolo’s counter-attacking threat.



CHRISTIAN PULISIC! ⚽#MilanLecce 1-0 pic.twitter.com/asefBjFFWe— Lega Serie A (@SerieA_EN) September 20, 2026 



Injuries could force Milan into tactical change



Milan will be without Alexis Saelemaekers, while Pervis Estupinan remains a fitness doubt after missing time with injury. Both players have been important options, leaving Amorim with decisions to make on the flanks. According to Gazzetta dello Sport, the circumstances could lead Amorim to field “his most attacking side ever”. 



The coach has generally avoided using two pure attacking wingers from the start, but the current selection problems could encourage him to take a different approach. The Neroverdi should provide a stern test for any tactical experiment. The hosts have already shown they can cause problems for stronger opponents, including a victory over Juventus.



AC Milan coach Ruben Amorim gestures



Will Pulisic play against Sassuolo and what role?



Amid the tactical uncertainty, Christian Pulisic is expected to start behind Goncalo Ramos if Amorim switches to a 4-2-3-1 formation. The American would operate as the central attacking midfielder, with Ramos leading the line and another attacking player occupying the wide left position.



That would represent a slight change from the alternative 3-4-2-1 system, in which Pulisic has also been projected to start alongside another attacking midfielder behind Ramos. Either way, the supplied lineup reports agree on one important point: the American remains one of the key attacking pieces in the coach’s plans.



How Milan could line up against Sassuolo as per La Gazzetta dello Sport



A possible 4-2-3-1 would feature Mike Maignan in goal, with Mario Gila and Strahinja Pavlovic involved in the defensive line and Davide Bartesaghi potentially replacing Estupinan. Samuel Chukwueze, Luka Modric and Adrien Rabiot would provide the midfield structure, while Pulisic would sit behind Ramos.



The 28-year-old forward could also benefit from the form of the players around him. Goncalo Ramos returned from international duty with three goals in four appearances for Portugal, while Alphadjo Cisse also scored for Italy Under-21.

items.title: Cristiano Ronaldo’s mother sends warning to Portugal in defence of her son’s legacy as Jorge Jesus rift continues
items.description:
Cristiano Ronaldo's departure from the Portugal national team has taken an emotional turn following public comments from his mother, Maria Dolores Aveiro. 
The circumstances surrounding Cristiano Ronaldo’s sudden exit from the Portugal national team have evolved following recent public statements from his mother, Maria Dolores Aveiro. In a television interview, she addressed the ongoing fallout resulting from her son’s dispute with manager Jorge Jesus. These comments arrive at a highly sensitive juncture for the 41-year-old forward, whose abrupt exit from the training camp has generated significant scrutiny regarding his continued involvement in international soccer.



The episode has already produced a disciplinary case and a public explanation from Ronaldo, who apologized for his actions while insisting that he remains available to represent Portugal. Now, his mother has offered her own perspective on how the situation has affected the family and how she believes her son’s extraordinary contribution should be viewed.



Dolores Aveiro admitted that Ronaldo’s departure from the Portugal camp was extremely difficult for her to process. Speaking to TV 7 Dias, she described the episode as a shock and revealed that she became emotional after learning that her son had left the squad.



“I feel sad, and that’s natural. It was a shock. My son could have left through the front door, but he left through the back door. But it’s okay; God will take care of everything. I cried a little. Sometimes crying is good to help us release what we’re feeling. We have to get through this phase.”



Cristiano Ronaldo #7 of Portugal reacts



She also revealed that she called Ronaldo shortly after he left the camp. According to Dolores, her son tried to reassure her that he would eventually explain his side of the story, while she encouraged him to remain calm during the difficult period.



Dolores Aveiro delivers her strongest message



The most striking part of Dolores’ comments was her defense of Ronaldo’s place in Portuguese football history. She believes her son has given enormous amounts to the national team and feels that his contribution has not received the recognition she believes it deserves.



“Cristiano has given so much to Portugal, and he will always be there. He has always been Portugal’s hero, but they don’t give him the recognition he deserves. They don’t appreciate Cristiano the way they should. This is the Portuguese we have.”



Cristiano Ronaldo of Portugal holds the UEFA Nations League trophy 



The comments add another emotional layer to a dispute that has already become one of the biggest stories surrounding the national team. Dolores’ words suggest that, from the Ronaldo family’s perspective, the issue extends beyond one disagreement over playing time and touches on how the captain’s legacy is being treated.



Ronaldo’s legacy now part of the debate



The disagreement with Jesus has inevitably shifted attention toward the final stage of Ronaldo’s Portugal career. At 41, he remains the national team’s all-time leading scorer and one of the defining figures in its history, while his international career already includes the 2016 European Championship and more than two decades of service.



Cristiano Ronaldo of Portugal holds the Euro 2016 trophy



For Dolores, that history should carry considerable weight when Ronaldo’s treatment is discussed. Her emotional intervention reflects the frustration within the player’s family, while Borges’ comments show that even those outside the immediate dispute continue to view Ronaldo’s legacy as something far bigger than one difficult international window.



Whether Ronaldo and Jesus can repair their relationship remains uncertain. For now, though, Ronaldo has left the door open to Portugal, his mother has made clear how strongly she feels about his treatment, and the debate over how one of the country’s greatest-ever players should be remembered has only intensified.

items.title: Cristiano Ronaldo’s entourage reportedly delivered major ultimatum to Jorge Jesus as Portugal crisis takes another turn
items.description:
A close friend of Jesus claims that Ronaldo's entourage made a major demand during the dispute, putting further pressure on a relationship that had already deteriorated over playing-time promises. 
The Cristiano Ronaldo and Jorge Jesus feud is completely blowing up with a massive new allegation. A close friend of Jesus claims that Ronaldo’s entourage made a major demand during the dispute, putting further pressure on a relationship that had already deteriorated over playing-time promises.



The allegation was made by Carlos Padrao, a former goalkeeper and close associate of Jesus, during an appearance on SIC Notícias’ Jogo Aberto. According to Padrao, Tiago Craveiro, a strategic consultant for Ronaldo’s company CR7 SA, contacted someone within Jesus’ circle as the disagreement intensified.



The controversy started during Portugal‘s UEFA Nations League campaign in September. Ronaldo had reportedly agreed to a plan regarding his playing time, but he was left on the bench against Norway on September 27 despite being told he would feature for around 30 minutes.



The 41-year-old warmed up during the second half but was never introduced as the Selecao won 2-1. Ronaldo subsequently accused Jesus of breaking his word and later explained that the dispute was about trust rather than a demand to play every match.



Cristiano Ronaldo of Portugal.



Ronaldo then left Portugal’s training camp before the next fixture and released a lengthy statement explaining his decision. He claimed that Jesus had broken two separate agreements, including a later understanding about how the coach would publicly explain the situation.



Ronaldo’s entourage allegedly issued stark ultimatum



That dispute has now produced an even more serious allegation. Padrao claims that Craveiro threatened that Jesus would be dismissed unless he publicly apologized to Ronaldo, with the alleged demand being delivered through someone close to the coach rather than directly to Jesus.



According to Padrao, Ronaldo’s camp even attempted to prepare a specific script for the Portugal coach to read at the beginning of a press conference. “They tried to create a script for Jorge Jesus to apologize to Cristiano Ronaldo,” Padrao told SIC Notícias.



The experienced boss reportedly refused to follow the script or issue the requested formal apology. Instead, he acknowledged that his handling of Ronaldo’s warm-up against Norway had been a mistake while maintaining a distinction between admitting an error and apologizing.



Cristiano Ronaldo of Portugal.



“Admitting a mistake is one thing, apologizing is another,” Padrao said, describing Jesus’ position. He also claimed that the coach is deeply saddened by the entire episode and remains affected by the deterioration of his relationship with Ronaldo.



Jesus previously had strong relationship with Ronaldo



The situation is particularly striking because Jesus and Ronaldo had recently worked together at Al-Nassr. The pair won the Saudi Pro League title together, and their relationship appeared to be strong before Jesus was appointed Portugal coach following the 2026 World Cup.



Cristiano Ronaldo and Jorge Jesus



Padrao has suggested that Jesus believed he could manage Ronaldo’s playing time precisely because of their previous relationship. The coach had also reportedly played a role in persuading Ronaldo to continue his international career after Portugal’s World Cup elimination by Spain.



That history makes the current disagreement more complicated. According to Padrao, Jesus never intended to create a confrontation with Ronaldo, and his friend believes the coach remains deeply disappointed that their relationship has reached this point.

items.title: Vinicius Junior’s market value takes another hit as struggles mount for Real Madrid and Brazil
items.description:
Vinicius Junior is going through one of the most difficult stretches of his career, and the numbers are now starting to reflect it. Between a slow start to the season at Real Madrid and a quiet international break with Brazil, the forward has seen the criticism around his performances grow on both fronts, and Transfermarkt's […] 
Vinicius Junior is going through one of the most difficult stretches of his career, and the numbers are now starting to reflect it. Between a slow start to the season at Real Madrid and a quiet international break with Brazil, the forward has seen the criticism around his performances grow on both fronts, and Transfermarkt’s latest update has made that decline official by lowering his market value to its lowest point in nearly four years.



According to the latest update, Vinicius is now valued at €130 million, which is €10 million less than his previous valuation and a drop of €70 million from the €200 million he reached in October 2024, shortly after helping Real Madrid win the Champions League.



The reduction comes as the 26-year-old struggles to find his best level for both club and country. For Real Madrid, he has scored just one goal in eight matches this season, to go with three assists in 652 minutes, and the criticism intensified after the 2-1 derby defeat to Atlético Madrid, when Yan Diomandé replaced him before the hour mark and made an immediate impact.



With Brazil, the picture has not been much brighter: he converted a late penalty in the 4-2 win over Australia, but the performance was far from a standout one, and a week earlier he had a forgettable hour in the 1-1 draw in Townsville before being substituted.



Vinicius Jr. of Brazil. (Getty Images)



Even so, Vinicius continues to have the full backing of the people who coach him. Carlo Ancelotti said after the win over Australia that “Vini Jr. deserves my patience” and that, even when he is not at his best, “he can still make the difference“. José Mourinho has also kept him in the starting lineup at Madrid despite the criticism, and the club recently reinforced its confidence in the forward by extending his contract until 2032, only two months ago.


        


From €200 million to €130 million in two years



Vinícius’ valuation reached its peak at €200 million in October 2024, after a season in which he helped Real Madrid win the Champions League. His value has been falling gradually since mid-2025, and this is the lowest figure attached to his name since November 2022, when he stood at €120 million just before the World Cup in Qatar, although at that time his price was on the rise rather than in decline.



DateMarket valueNovember 2022€120 millionJune 2023€150 millionDecember 2023€150 millionJune 2024€180 millionOctober 2024€200 millionDecember 2024€200 millionJune 2025€170 millionOctober 2025€150 millionDecember 2025€150 millionJune 2026€140 millionOctober 2026€130 million



Vinícius’ poor run could also open the door for other attacking options at Real Madrid. Yan Diomandé’s valuation jumped from €90 million to €120 million, the biggest increase in LaLiga, while Arda Güler reached €100 million for the first time, and both are in a position to take advantage if the Brazilian’s struggles continue.

Inter Miami reportedly plan long-term future with Lionel Messi after Argentina retirement
items.description:
Since Lionel Messi arrived in 2023, Inter Miami have grown from a promising MLS franchise into the league's most valuable club. 
Inter Miami are already planning a long-term future with Lionel Messi that goes well beyond his current contract, according to reports. Now that the 39-year-old has retired from the Argentina national team, he is fully focused on the MLS, and the club’s ownership want to keep him tied to the franchise even after he stops playing, a vision that includes the possibility of him becoming a shareholder.



Messi’s contract with Inter Miami runs through the end of the 2028 MLS season, but the club’s leadership do not want that date to mark the end of the relationship. Jorge Mas, the team’s managing owner and CEO, considers that the project built around Messi requires an investment of between $70 million and $80 million per year, taking into account all the elements linked to the player.



Xavier Asensi, the club’s president of business operations, has also revealed that Inter Miami already contemplate the scenario after Messi’s retirement and the chance that he can become part of the club’s ownership group once he stops playing professionally. BBC Sport reported that his agreement already includes a pathway to receive a minority stake in the team after his playing career ends, and that Messi prefers the idea of owning a club to coaching one.



Even so, nothing has been signed yet: there is no confirmed agreement to extend Messi’s contract through 2030, a date that for now should be understood as a long-term horizon and not as a closed renewal. For the moment, Messi’s immediate focus will be on the field, with Inter Miami set to host DC United on Saturday, October 10, at Nu Stadium in the MLS regular season.



Lionel Messi celebrates a goal for Inter Miami. (Getty Images)



How Messi turned Inter Miami into MLS’s most valuable club



Since Lionel Messi arrived in July 2023, Inter Miami have gone from a young franchise with promise to the league’s biggest commercial force. The club was valued at around $600 million before his signing, and Forbes now puts that figure at $1.35 billion, making Inter Miami the most valuable team in MLS ahead of LAFC.


        


The growth has come with trophies as well: the 2023 Leagues Cup, the 2024 Supporters’ Shield and the 2025 MLS Cup, a 3-1 win over Vancouver in which Messi provided an assist.



That growth explains why Inter Miami want to keep him for as long as possible. Keeping Messi reportedly costs the club between $70 and $80 million a year, according to Mas, but the commercial return has so far outweighed that investment. With much of the club’s recent value tied to his presence, Inter Miami are reportedly working on a long-term plan that would keep him involved beyond his playing career, including a potential path to a shareholder role.
